title: There are no Collatz m-cycles with m ≤ 91
notes: Journal of Integer Sequences 26 (2023) Article 23.3.5. Proves every nontrivial Collatz m-cycle has m≥92, where m is the number of local minima. Valley arrangement carries cycle information beyond (K,L) parity counts; the argument is Diophantine, not spectral. Cited from docs/problems/juggler_cycle_word_functional.md. READ FROM THE PDF, 19 September 2026 (docs/problems/juggler_collatz_finance_mirror.md): Definition 4 takes the floor X_0 = 695 * 2^60; the introduction attributes the period bound K > 7.2e10 odd steps to Hercher and Puchert 2018 (hercher-2018-collatz-cycle-length); Lemma 8 is the 2-adic run congruence, k consecutive odd steps force n = -1 mod 2^k hence n >= 2^k - 1; Theorem 16 is the finance identity 2^(K+L) = product over odd n of (3 + 1/n) with T(n_i) the reciprocal sum over a run; Corollary 17 gives sum T(n_i) <= (97/54) m/X_0; Theorem 27 gives sum T(n_i) <= (3/4) K/X_0 independently of m via Lemma 26's averaging over at most three consecutive runs; Corollary 29 reaches X_0 >= 1536 * 2^60 by tracking residue classes modulo powers of two computationally. CORRECTION to the earlier sentence 'the Juggler run-type count e is the analogous valley count': Paper A's Theorem 3.31 bounds the number of even letters by a census of run forms, while Hercher bounds the number of local minima by a Diophantine argument; the Juggler m-cycle problem is open for every m, including m = 1 (J-cycle-gaps-are-mirror-images, J-collatz-walk-charge-constant). THE FINAL SECTION, placed 20 September 2026: it proves that to raise the odd-step count of a nontrivial cycle to the next bound, K >= 1.375 * 10^11, it suffices to verify convergence for every integer up to 1536 * 2^60 = 3 * 2^69 (Corollary 29, residue classes tracked modulo powers of two), nearly 60 percent less range than the finance-type bounds need; the abstract states 'Simons and de Weger proved m >= 76', 'with newer bounds ... m >= 83', and the paper's m >= 92. Barina 2025 (barina-2025-collatz-verification-limit) verified through 2^71 = 2048 * 2^60 and states the consequence, citing this paper: the length of a nontrivial cycle rises to 355504839929 in the standard count, i.e. 217976794617 shortcut steps with 137528045312 odd ones, the second survivor of Paper A's Theorem 5.18 at 2^71; the finance alone would keep the first survivor, 114208327604, until 2^71.88. Paper A's Theorem 5.18 records this since the 20 September evening edition. Whether m rises above 91 at 2^71 would need this paper's Diophantine analysis redone at the new floor; not done here.
